title: Volkswagen Dieselgate: defeat-device software, lab-field divergence, and regulator visibility rails
summary: Dieselgate is promoted as an intentional software-mediated regulatory-evasion record: internal software state detected official emissions testing and altered behavior, making laboratory compliance a poor witness for real-world emissions until independent in-use testing and regulator action exposed the divergence.

type_payload.incident_class: intentional software-mediated regulatory evasion / emissions defeat-device case
type_payload.system: Volkswagen/Audi/Porsche diesel engine control software and emissions compliance testing

sequence_of_events.event: Regulated vehicles used software that recognized emissions-test conditions.
The software turned full emissions controls on during testing and reduced effectiveness in normal driving.
Independent in-use testing by WVU/ICCT and regulator follow-up exposed the laboratory-field divergence.
Civil and criminal settlements/guilty plea followed, and EPA added defeat-device screening protocols.

type_payload.proximate_cause: A software algorithm intentionally changed emissions-control behavior when it detected official testing versus normal driving.

contributing_factors: regulator initially unable to infer real-world behavior from standard tests alone
corporate misconduct documented by official resolutions
latent_conditions: A software system can be designed to perform honesty toward the test rather than toward the world.
Compliance testing without adversarial/in-use rails can be gamed by state-sensitive code.
